slides.title: Kurt Lewin | Field Theory, Gestalt Psychology, Group Dynamics - Britannica
slides.highlight: This entry outlines Kurt Lewin's foundational theories on group dynamics and field theory, which provide the theoretical underpinnings for understanding collective human behavior and social perception.

slides.title: Simulating access to alcohol screening, brief intervention, referral to and receipt of specialty treatment for alcohol use disorder in California and Texas: A study protocol for an agent-based modeling study (AUDTxSim)
slides.tldr: Agent-based simulation of alcohol treatment access disparities
slides.highlight: This study employs a large-scale, spatially explicit agent-based model to simulate healthcare access and treatment dynamics for alcohol use disorder, offering a methodological framework for analyzing societal-scale health interventions and equity outcomes relevant to MIMIC's focus on multi-scale societal simulation.

card.one_liner: Agent-based model simulating alcohol treatment access and outcomes in California and Texas populations.
card.key_idea: Stochastic, spatially explicit simulation of 47 million agents modeling SBIRT, facility capacity, and treatment transitions.
card.evaluation: Protocol only; no results reported. Plans calibration to census/NSDUH data and projection of policy scenarios.
card.limitation: Excludes migration and natural population growth; relies on placeholder parameters pending calibration.

slides.title: Robots That Talk Too Much and Don't Listen Enough
slides.highlight: The paper argues that multimodal bidirectional streaming is essential to reduce turn-taking failures in social robot interactions, a key challenge for HyECHO's goal of robust hybrid human-AI team state perception.

card.one_liner: Bidirectional multimodal streaming reduces turn-taking failures in social robots by enabling simultaneous listening and speaking.
card.key_idea: Implementing bidirectional audio and video streaming allows robots to process user input while speaking, detecting interruptions and facial cues.
card.evaluation: Qualitative analysis of dialogue transcripts and object recognition tests using Google ADK and Furhat robots; no quantitative metrics provided.
card.limitation: Evaluation is anecdotal and qualitative, lacking rigorous benchmarks or statistical evidence of reduced failure rates.

slides.title: Alleviating Interview Stress: Effects of Robot Persona and Reactive Backchanneling on High-Pressure Mock Interviews
slides.tldr: ROBOT PERSONA AND BACKCHANNELING IN MOCK INTERVIEWS
slides.highlight: This study examines how robot interviewer personas and nonverbal backchanneling affect user anxiety and social presence, offering insights relevant to designing supportive embodied social robots for high-pressure interactions.

card.one_liner: Supportive robot personas reduce stress, while active backchanneling unexpectedly increases anxiety in mock interviews.
card.key_idea: 2x2 experiment testing robot persona (supportive/challenging) and backchanneling (active/negative) effects on anxiety and facial expressions.
card.evaluation: N=28 between-subjects study with NAO robot; measured state anxiety, self-efficacy, and facial emotion recognition.
card.limitation: Small sample size (N=28) and preliminary nature limit generalizability and statistical power.

slides.title: Social Signal Bench: Evidence-Weighted Evaluation of Co-occurring Social Signals in Video and Audio
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a densely annotated benchmark and an evidence-weighted metric for evaluating co-occurring social signals and engagement in multimodal conversations, directly supporting HyECHO's goal of robust social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Introduces a 47-hour benchmark and Evidence-Weighted F1 metric for evaluating co-occurring social signals in video and audio.
card.key_idea: Proposes EW-F1, which weights labels by annotator evidence and grants partial credit for semantically related signals via taxonomy-based matching.
card.evaluation: Tested on 47-hour dataset; post-trained 7B models outperform frontier baselines on video and match them on audio using EW-F1.
card.limitation: Labels reflect expert perception rather than ground truth; results limited to English, single-speaker contexts with few test recordings per domain.

slides.title: Nunchi: Ears Help Eyes in Multi-Party Conversations
slides.highlight: This work addresses the ambiguity of gaze geometry in multi-party settings by integrating speech and transcript cues, directly supporting HyECHO's goal of robust addressee modeling and social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Nunchi combines gaze geometry with conversational cues in a VLM to identify attended persons in multi-party scenes.
card.key_idea: Constructs text prompts from gaze heatmaps, speaker scores, and transcripts, using shared labels to align cues for VLM reasoning.
card.evaluation: Tested on new SORBET benchmark and existing datasets; outperforms baselines by 4.8 points, with gains holding across three VLMs.
card.limitation: Relies on scripted TV data and single keyframes; struggles with gaze shifts, off-screen targets, and cross-dataset transfer.

slides.title: Alibaba Releases Qwen4-Max with Cybersecurity Guardrails
slides.highlight: Alibaba has released Qwen4-Max, a large language model distinguished by its implementation of strict cybersecurity guardrails.

slides.title: It's My Turn! Interpretable Methods Reveal Developmental Differences from Mother-Child Conversational Dynamics
slides.highlight: This study introduces an interpretable computational framework combining sequence analysis and Bayesian modeling to characterize temporal conversational dynamics and serve-and-return patterns in parent-child interactions. It is relevant to HyECHO as it demonstrates methods for modeling group norms and engagement through reciprocal turn-taking dynamics without relying on data-hungry approaches.

card.one_liner: Interpretable models reveal that higher developmental scores correlate with more organized, predictable mother-child turn-taking.
card.key_idea: Combines sequence analysis, mutual information, and Bayesian hierarchical modeling to characterize temporal conversational dynamics in parent-child play.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 94 mother-child dyads using Bayley scores; results show structural differences but lack statistical significance in predictability metrics.
card.limitation: Small sample size, reliance on manual annotation, and overlapping confidence intervals limit statistical confidence in developmental differences.

slides.highlight: NVIDIA announced GR00T 2 and other robot technologies at the CoRL Conference.

slides.title: Microsoft Releases MAI Code 2 AI Model
slides.highlight: Microsoft has released MAI Code 2, a new AI model focused on code generation.

slides.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
slides.highlight: This review highlights the shift from passive monitoring to agentic robotics, emphasizing that embodiment, governance, and human oversight are critical for integrating robots into care ecosystems.

card.one_liner: Agentic robotics for care remains immature, requiring embodied AI and strict governance for safe clinical integration.
card.key_idea: Proposes agentic robotics to bridge remote monitoring and action, emphasizing embodiment, interoperable architectures, and auditable human oversight.
card.evaluation: Structured scoping review finding most systems remain human-led prototypes with limited decision-action coupling and embodied AI.
card.limitation: Mature agentic care is absent; current systems lack validated workflows, strong decision-action coupling, and robust governance frameworks.

slides.title: Measuring Public Participation in Local Government: An Audio-Based Instrument for Classifying Speakers in City Council Meetings
slides.tldr: AUDIO-BASED SPEAKER CLASSIFICATION FOR PUBLIC PARTICIPATION METRICS
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates a pipeline for speaker diarization and role classification (official vs. public) using multimodal LLMs and temporal context, directly supporting HyECHO's goal of non-data-hungry multimodal social perception and addressee modeling in hybrid group settings.

card.one_liner: An audio-based pipeline classifies city council speakers to measure public participation without transcription.
card.key_idea: Combines speaker diarization with a multimodal LLM using temporal context and iterative bootstrapping to classify officials versus public participants.
card.evaluation: Validated on 1,761 human-annotated speakers across five cities; achieves 87.7% accuracy and 89% diarization accuracy with high inter-rater reliability.
card.limitation: Sample is non-representative (urban, Democratic-leaning cities); accuracy relies on Gemini 2.5 Flash and may degrade with poor audio quality.

slides.title: Marimba: A System One Model for Speech
slides.highlight: Marimba demonstrates that frozen ASR features can support lightweight, non-data-hungry heads for critical social perception tasks like speaker diarization and turn completion, aligning with HyECHO's goal of efficient multimodal state modeling.

card.one_liner: Marimba uses a frozen ASR encoder to answer typed speech decisions like term spotting and turn detection.
card.key_idea: Routes lexical queries to zero-shot ASR transcript scoring and non-lexical tasks to a question-conditioned head or frozen layer readouts.
card.evaluation: Tested on public and private conversational sets; achieves high AUROC for terms and speakers, but turn-end detection trails dedicated baselines.
card.limitation: Lexical accuracy inherits ASR errors on rare terms; scene classification fails; term detection latency is high (2.35s) due to decoding.

slides.title: Talk to Act: A Synthetic Multi-Turn Dialogue Benchmark for Human Intent Extraction and Action Planning in Robotics
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a synthetic multi-turn dialogue benchmark to evaluate small, open-weight language models for intent extraction and action planning in robotics. It is relevant to RwB as it demonstrates that compact, locally deployable models can serve as a useful baseline for conversational human-robot interaction without task-specific fine-tuning.

card.one_liner: A synthetic multi-turn dialogue benchmark evaluates small open-weight LLMs for robotic intent extraction and action planning.
card.key_idea: Generates 977 synthetic dialogues with structured JSON annotations for actions and objects, framing intent extraction as a tool-calling problem.
card.evaluation: Benchmarks five small models (270M–8B) on goal accuracy and action F1; Gemma4:E4B achieves 63.6% goal accuracy without fine-tuning.
card.limitation: Relies on synthetic data which may lack real-world nuance; current performance suggests significant room for improvement via fine-tuning.

slides.title: LanceDB: The data layer for multimodal AI
slides.highlight: LanceDB provides a data layer for multimodal AI, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid human-AI team states.

slides.title: Symmetries of Counterfactuals: Identification and Testability of Counterfactual Maps from Covariate Heterogeneity
slides.highlight: This work provides a rigorous framework for identifying and testing counterfactual maps using covariate heterogeneity, addressing a core challenge in causal inference relevant to MIMIC's need for reliable counterfactual reasoning in hybrid human-AI society simulations.

card.one_liner: Covariate heterogeneity identifies counterfactual symmetries and enables testing structural causal model assumptions.
card.key_idea: Characterizes counterfactual maps via symmetry groups preserving conditional distributions; proposes a conditional independence test for model class validity.
card.evaluation: Validated on synthetic data and ACTG 175 HIV trial; test rejects invalid maps but cannot distinguish between triangular monotone and optimal transport classes.
card.limitation: Requires covariates influencing latent causes; low heterogeneity yields large symmetry groups, limiting identifiability and test power.

slides.title: Hesai Kosmo and Ropedia Partner on End-to-End Embodied AI Training Data Pipeline
slides.highlight: The partnership between Hesai Kosmo and Ropedia establishes an end-to-end pipeline for generating training data for embodied AI, a critical infrastructure component for advancing the capabilities of social robots and human-robot interaction systems.
